taxonomy.subtopic: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency and persistence of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers

questions.stem_html: A 36-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department for fluctuating confusion and petechiae. Hemoglobin is 8.1 g/dL, platelet count is 18,000/mm³, creatinine is mildly elevated, and the reticulocyte count is increased. The blood smear shows fragmented erythrocytes. Prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time are normal. The accompanying diagram shows unusually long endothelial von Willebrand factor strings binding platelets. Loss of which activity most directly produces this process?

options.text_html: Proteolytic cleavage of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers
Endothelial release of tissue plasminogen activator
Gamma-carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors
Cross-linking of fibrin by activated factor XIII

questions.explanation_html: ADAMTS13 normally cleaves ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers released from endothelium. Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, most often due to an acquired inhibitor, permits highly adhesive multimers to persist and recruit platelets in small vessels. Platelet-rich microthrombi cause thrombocytopenia, organ ischemia, and shearing of passing erythrocytes into schistocytes. Coagulation times remain normal because systemic consumption of coagulation factors is not the primary process.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Impaired gamma-carboxylation prolongs coagulation times and causes a coagulation-factor bleeding disorder rather than platelet-rich microangiopathic thrombosis.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Factor XIII cross-links fibrin after clot formation; deficiency causes delayed bleeding with otherwise normal routine coagulation tests, not schistocytic hemolysis and severe thrombocytopenia.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Reduced tissue plasminogen activator would decrease fibrinolysis but does not explain ultra-large von Willebrand factor strings.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Reduced thromboxane synthesis impairs platelet aggregation and causes bleeding; it would not produce spontaneous platelet-rich microthrombi.

questions.educational_objective: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency allows ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers to persist, causing platelet-rich microthrombi, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.
